newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH MINISTER PROMISES RADICAL UNEMPLOYMENT CUT.
newsitem.headline: POLISH MINISTER PROMISES RADICAL UNEMPLOYMENT CUT.

text.p: Poland's jobless rate should fall radically next year thanks to job-creation programmes and new legislation aimed to clamp down on the widespread abuse of the unemployment system, the labour minister said on Friday.
"Next year we should see a radical fall in unemployment as a result of active fight against unemployment...and a new unemployment bill," Andrzej Baczkowski told a news conference.
Earlier in the day the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said registered unemployment fell to 13.5 percent of the workforce in September from 13.8 percent in August and 15 percent a year ago.
But Baczkowski said that if abuses of the unemployment law were eliminated the actual unemployment would be already much lower.
"The actual unemployment in Poland would be about 10 percent if cases of abuse were eliminated," he said.

The new bill, approved by the government last month, would make it harder to become eligible for unemployment benefits and would require recipients of benefits to actively seek employment to maintain their status.
Baczkowski earlier said that if the new regulations became law, the national budget spending on unemployment benefits would be cut by 420 million zlotys next year.
Most of the sum would be spent on creating new jobs and on vocational trainings, he added.
Parliament will debate the draft law at its session next week and is likely to approve it by the end of the year.
